note: Seed 303 stalled for 88 s at a 3-tile wall. The lookahead assumed Mario would hop on his own later, so 'run' tied with jumping. Both plans were also stopped at a fake wall, made by copying the last visible column past the tile window, and the tie-break against jumping put it off forever. Seeds 101 and 202 died because the only escape was pressing S just before touching down, and the rule 'never jump in the air unless boosting' forbade it. Changes: 1) The lookahead now tests one extra jump at each later decision. 2) Gain is now the average progress, so an earlier jump scores higher. 3) Each non-jump outcome now reports when its plan must jump (hop: none/next/later), and Mario jumps now when that is 'next'. 4) Beyond the visible tiles the level is assumed to be ground no higher than Mario. 5) jumpReady and boosting are replaced by a categorical jumpKey (start/boost/landing/wait), which allows a press that lands just after touch-down.

instructions:
Play the game well. Infinite Mario. Left and Right walk, S jumps (hold it for a higher jump), A runs (and throws fireballs with the fire flower), Down ducks. Run to the right through the level as far as you can: jump over pits and obstacles, stomp enemies by landing on them from above (touching one any other way hurts, and small Mario dies of it), avoid piranha plants and bullets. Reaching the end of the level wins it.
jumpKey tells what pressing S (the actions jump, jumpRight, runJumpRight) does now: start = on the ground, a jump starts; boost = rising in a jump that holding S still lifts; landing = in the air but touching down just before the press takes effect, so the press starts a jump right on landing; wait = pressing S now starts nothing, and holding it would block the next jump.
outcome[action] is a physics lookahead of about 0.9 s after the input lag. The action is held for one decision, then Mario keeps that direction and keeps S held while a jump still lifts. Mario may also start one more jump at a later decision, and the best of those plans is reported. fate: safe; stomp (lands on an enemy, which is fine); hurt (touches an enemy, piranha or bullet, and small Mario dies); pit (falls to death). t = ms until the harm when no plan avoids it. gain = tiles ahead of Mario's current position, averaged over the lookahead, so more progress made sooner scores higher. hop (non-jump actions only) = when that plan must start its jump: none, next (at the very next decision) or later.
Rules. When status is none, press jump or idle (equally good). When it is dying or won, idle. Otherwise:
1. When jumpKey is wait, never choose jump, jumpRight or runJumpRight.
2. Keep the remaining actions whose fate is safe or stomp. If there are none, take the remaining action with the largest t, counting a hurt as 5000 ms later when big is true (big Mario survives a hit).
3. When jumpKey is boost and a jump action is kept, keep only the jump actions (finish the jump).
4. Keep the actions whose gain is within 0.3 of the highest gain.
5. When jumpKey is start or landing: if a kept non-jump action has hop none or later, keep only those non-jump actions, so Mario jumps only when it helps. Otherwise, if any jump actions are kept, keep only those: a plan that needs its jump at the next decision should jump now.
6. Take the highest gain; actions within 0.1 of it are equally good.
threat (nearest danger), pitAhead/pitWidth and wallAhead/wallHeight (tiles from Mario's front) tell what the outcomes are reacting to.

actions.description: release every key: slow down and wait
run right with A held (fire Mario throws a fireball each time A is pressed again)
jump straight up, or keep holding jump to rise higher
jump while walking right, or keep holding jump
